findings.title: Rescheduling bookings uses immediateDelete, bypassing the deferred SendGrid cancellation fix
findings.body: `handleNewBooking.ts` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true` when rescheduling a booking. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `immediateDelete = true` immediately calls SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` endpoint instead of marking the reminder `cancelled: true` for the cron job to cancel within 1 hour of the send time, and it also returns early without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` record in the database. Rescheduled bookings will therefore still consume SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit right away (defeating the purpose of this PR for reschedules) and leave orphaned `workflowReminder` rows in the database.

findings.title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders`
findings.body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called at line 19, but `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is never called (unlike in `emailReminderManager.ts` line 26). Unless `emailReminderManager` happens to be imported in the same serverless instance prior to this endpoint running, `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` (and `/v3/mail/batch`) will fail with `401 Unauthorized` from SendGrid, preventing scheduled email reminders from being cancelled or scheduled by the cron job.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts all remaining cancellations and DB deletions
findings.body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop awaits `client.request(...)` for each reminder inside a single outer `try` block and defers all `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations to `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop. Note that Prisma's `.delete()` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that only executes when awaited. If any single `client.request` call throws (e.g., an invalid `batch_id` or transient SendGrid error), none of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted from the database and none of the subsequent reminders in the batch are processed. On the next cron run, the same failing reminder will be retried and block the queue again. Each iteration should have its own `try/catch` and `await` the DB delete immediately after its SendGrid call succeeds.

findings.title: Editing a workflow step queries already-cancelled reminders and overwrites `cancelled: true`
findings.body: In `workflows.tsx` inside the `update` mutation (line 507), `remindersFromStep` is fetched with `where: { workflowStepId: oldStep.id }` without filtering out `cancelled: true`. Earlier in the same mutation (lines 376-382), reminders for removed event types were marked `cancelled: true` via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (which is also not awaited, creating a race condition). In addition, reminders from previously cancelled bookings on that step also have `cancelled: true` in the DB. When `oldStep` is edited, `remindersToUpdate` (lines 567-580) will include those already-cancelled reminders; if `oldStep` is deleted (lines 519-525), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` will be called on already-cancelled reminders without deleting their DB rows. `remindersFromStep` should filter `NOT: { cancelled: true }` (or `cancelled: false`), and the async calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` should be awaited.
